claims.claim: For p not dividing the base b, collision detection is exactly repeated-state detection on mismatch-only normalized prefix sums. Moreover, every collision has a witness containing at most p mismatching aligned positions, although its length may exceed p.
claims.evidence: Let Δ_t=s[t]-s[t+d]. For 0≤r<e≤n-d, b^e(A_d(e)-A_d(r))=sum_{t=r}^{e-1} Δ_t b^{e-1-t}=F(r,e-r)-F(r+d,e-r) modulo p. Because p does not divide b, b^e is invertible, proving the exact state/fingerprint equivalence. A_d is constant on aligned equal runs. Numbering mismatches q_1<...<q_m and setting B_0=0, B_j=A_d(q_j+1), any genuine collision canonically yields B_a=B_c for a<c, and every such repetition yields unequal substrings containing exactly c-a mismatches. If m≥p, two of B_0,...,B_p coincide by pigeonhole; if m<p, every interval contains fewer than p mismatches. This proves the bounded witness statement. Exhaustive exact checks agreed for every aligned interval in the tested corpus.
claims.witness: For any repetition B_a=B_c with a<c, take r=0 when a=0 and r=q_a+1 otherwise, and take e=q_c+1. The substrings S[r..e) and S[r+d..e+d) are unequal, have equal fingerprints, and contain exactly c-a≤p mismatches for the pigeonhole-selected pair.
claims.search_method: Universal algebraic derivation followed by exhaustive integer-arithmetic enumeration of all strings over bases 2 through length 9, 3 through length 7, and 4 through length 6, using primes 2,3,5,7,11 whenever p does not divide b.

claims.claim: In the word-RAM model with p=n^{O(1)}, there is an exact deterministic algorithm running in O(n log n+n+min{D,M,n min(n,p)}) time, where D is the number of distinct substring contents and M is the number of unequal unordered character-position pairs. Consequently the requested O(n log n) bound holds when p=O(log n), D=O(n log n), or M=O(n log n).
claims.evidence: For p not dividing b, deterministic suffix-array/LCP/RMQ preprocessing supports constant-time LCE jumps. At displacement d these enumerate the first min(m_d,p) mismatches. Reaching p mismatches certifies a collision by claim 0; otherwise every mismatch state has been enumerated and duplicate (d,state) keys decide the displacement exactly. The record count is Q=O(n+sum_d min(m_d,p)). Each unequal unordered position pair contributes to exactly one displacement, so sum_d m_d=M=(n^2-sum_c n_c^2)/2, while sum_d min(n-d,p)=O(n min(n,p)). Hence Q=O(n+min{M,n min(n,p)}). Since p=n^{O(1)}, the keys occupy O(log n) bits and deterministic constant-pass radix sorting costs O(n+Q). Independently, the compact suffix tree has one unit edge position per distinct substring content, totaling D; traversing those positions computes one fingerprint per content in O(D), and duplicate (length,fingerprint) keys are exactly unequal-content collisions. D is computable from edge-depth increments before choosing the cheaper route. If p divides b, the endpoint algorithm audited in claim 2 is already O(n log n), within the stated bound. The three stated O(n log n) consequences follow immediately. Exact enumeration matched both decision routes to brute force and verified the M identity and periodic-content bound.
claims.witness: A positive certificate is either two records with the same (d,state), the first p+1 states at a displacement, or two distinct substring contents with the same (length,fingerprint). A negative result after full applicable enumeration excludes every collision by the proved equivalences.
claims.search_method: Derived the record accounting and both exact decision routes, then exhaustively compared them against brute-force collision detection on 48,805 string/prime instances; 39,044 were invertible-base instances. All counting used integers.

claims.claim: The target has a complete O(n log n) exact solution in the noninvertible case p divides b.
claims.evidence: When p divides b, a nonempty most-significant-first fingerprint is its last character modulo p. For endpoints e<f in the same residue class, every admissible pair of equal-length ending substrings is equal exactly when R_e=s[e]...s[0] is a prefix of R_f=s[f]...s[0]. If the prefix relation fails after t matching characters, length t+1 gives an unequal colliding pair. Ordering endpoints within each residue class gives strings of increasing length; therefore all pairs satisfy the prefix relation iff every consecutive pair does, by transitivity. Exact LCP support on the reversed string takes O(n log n) preprocessing and O(1) per consecutive test, for O(n log n) total time. Reversing the orientation handles the opposite coefficient convention. Exhaustive comparison with brute force passed on 9,761 noninvertible instances in both orientations.
claims.witness: For a consecutive residue-class pair e<f whose backward LCP has length t<e+1, the length-(t+1) substrings ending at e and f are a concrete unequal colliding pair.
claims.search_method: Proved the endpoint-prefix characterization and transitive consecutive-pair reduction, then exhaustively checked all noninvertible cases in the finite corpus against brute force for both coefficient orientations.

claims.claim: Collisions cannot occur at length L when b^L<=p, but checking only power-of-two lengths, only lexicographically adjacent contents, or relying on monotonicity in the length is insufficient.
claims.evidence: Two distinct canonical length-L base-b words are distinct integers in [0,b^L-1], so their nonzero difference has absolute value at most b^L-1
claims.witness: b=2, p=5, S=000101: contents 000 and 101 have integer values 0 and 5 and collide modulo 5 only at length 3; their lexicographic ranks are first and fourth.
claims.search_method: Exact injectivity proof plus direct integer evaluation of the stated example and exhaustive threshold tests over all 48,805 string/prime instances in the corpus.

target_evidence: The exact target requests a worst-case O(n log n) or linear detector for an arbitrary supplied string and prime, with a declared small false-rejection probability permitted. The draft proves a complete exact solution when p divides b and exact O(n log n) solutions in several invertible-base regimes, together with useful structural reductions. It does not provide the requested bound in the general p-not-dividing-b case when none of p=O(log n), D=O(n log n), or M=O(n log n) applies; its displayed adaptive bound can then be superlinear. The final writeup explicitly identifies this uncovered case and claims only partial resolution. The progress is material and correctly scoped, so target coverage is VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS and the draft's claimed_resolution of PARTIAL is ACCURATE.
